name: Shoulder-width training (lateral raises, delts)
summary: Building the side delts, mostly with lateral raises, to make the frame look wider; muscle can change visible width but not bone width.
lead: Shoulder-width training is a looksmaxxing practice in which people train the deltoid muscles, most often with lateral raises, to make the shoulders appear wider. It is discussed in the looksmax.org community as part of improving frame and proportions, and members regularly post their "bideltoid" measurements and ask how they compare with the general population at a given height .
claims: Lateral raises can make the shoulders visibly broader.
Bideltoid size should be compared against height to judge whether the shoulders are narrow.
Heavy or very high-volume shoulder work carries injury risk.

name: V-taper / shoulder-to-waist ratio
summary: The broad-shoulders, narrow-waist silhouette that lifters and looksmaxxers treat as the male physique ideal, usually quoted as a ratio near 1.6.
lead: The V-taper is a physique in which broad shoulders and a wide upper back narrow down to a slim waist, giving an inverted-triangle silhouette. It is a long-standing ideal in bodybuilding and is discussed in looksmaxxing as the shoulder-to-waist ratio .
claims: A shoulder-to-waist ratio of about 1.6 is the ideal.
A narrow waist comes from fat loss, not abdominal exercise.
Broad shoulders with a narrow waist signal dominance and attractiveness.

name: Biacromial / clavicle width
summary: The bone-based width of the shoulder girdle, which looksmaxxers treat as a fixed frame limit that muscle can only add to.
lead: Biacromial width, the span across the acromion processes of the shoulder blades, and clavicle length are discussed in looksmaxxing as the bone-set limits on shoulder width. Members commonly say that training can add muscle on the outside of this frame but cannot change the skeleton .
claims: Clavicle width sets the ceiling for how wide the shoulders can look.
Specific bideltoid numbers (for example 24 inches) define a high-status frame.

name: Clavicle lengthening osteotomy
summary: A rare, extreme surgery floated on forums to widen the shoulders by cutting and lengthening the collarbones; no cosmetic studies found.
lead: Clavicle lengthening osteotomy refers to a surgical procedure in which the collarbone is cut and lengthened with the aim of widening the shoulders. It appears in looksmaxxing circles as a rare, extreme hardmaxxing option and is not an established cosmetic operation.

name: Stomach vacuum / waist training
summary: Pulling the belly in to train the deep abdominal muscle for a smaller-looking waist; little research exists on it for appearance.
lead: The stomach vacuum is an abdominal exercise in which the stomach is pulled inward, discussed in looksmaxxing as a way to make the waist look smaller. It is associated with the transversus abdominis, the deepest of the four muscles of the front abdominal wall .
claims: The stomach vacuum skill can be lost and regained with training.

name: Neckmaxxing / neck training
summary: Building a thicker neck to improve frame and jaw proportions; discussed with ratio targets that no published study validates.
lead: Neckmaxxing is the looksmaxxing practice of training the neck to make it thicker, on the belief that a wider neck contributes to a masculine, dominant look and better facial and frame proportions .
claims: A neck about as wide as the jaw is ideal.
Neck training can add notable rating points to overall looks.
Neck training is risky.

name: Grip and forearm training
summary: Targeted work for the hands and forearms to build grip strength and forearm size; popular for the look of the arms, with little direct research on appearance.
lead: Grip and forearm training refers to exercise aimed at the muscles of the forearm and hand, which produce wrist movement and gripping force. Practitioners use movements such as wrist curls, dead hangs, loaded carries and gripper devices, and in strength sports grip is also treated as a performance factor in pulling lifts.
claims: Pulling and hanging exercises build the forearms without direct wrist work.
Dedicated forearm training makes the forearms bigger and stronger.
Thicker forearms make a person look more masculine or attractive.

name: Calisthenics / gymnast physique
summary: Building a lean, muscular, gymnast-style frame through bodyweight training; popular as a low-cost route to size, with direct evidence on its aesthetic results limited.
lead: Calisthenics, also called bodyweight exercise, is strength training that uses the body's own weight for resistance and typically requires little or no equipment . Its name derives from Greek words for beauty and strength . Common exercises include push-ups, pull-ups, dips, squats and planks, while advanced skills include handstands, front and back levers, muscle-ups and the planche .
claims: Calisthenics can build serious muscle if done like a bodybuilding program.
Legs are hard to grow with bodyweight alone.
High-volume calisthenics is better than weight lifting.

name: Ring training / planche progressions
summary: Gymnastic-style strength work on rings and planche holds; a skill-based route to upper-body size with no appearance studies behind it.
lead: Gymnastic rings are two rings hung from a frame by straps, used in men's artistic gymnastics. A standard apparatus has rings with an 18 cm inner diameter hung 300 cm from the attachment point . Elements include strength holds such as the iron cross and Maltese cross, and swing elements such as giant swings .

name: Dirty bulk / lean bulk
summary: Two ways of eating in a calorie surplus to gain size: a large, loosely tracked surplus versus a small, controlled one.
lead: Bulking is the bodybuilding practice of eating in a calorie surplus to build muscle, usually followed by a cutting phase in a deficit . Wikipedia says competitive bodybuilders spend most of the year in an off-season build and cut for roughly 12 to 14 weeks before a contest .
claims: A small, tracked surplus lets you add muscle without getting fat.
Dirty bulking is a faster way to gain size.

name: Anabolic diet / high calorie eating
summary: A cyclic low-carbohydrate bodybuilding diet from the 1990s, often grouped with heavy-eating approaches to gaining size; no appearance studies found.
lead: The Anabolic Diet is a cyclic ketogenic diet (CKD) published in 1995 by Mauro Di Pasquale, and it was nicknamed the Pork Chop Diet . Di Pasquale, born in 1945, is an Italian-born Canadian powerlifter and writer who won the IPF World Powerlifting Championships in 1976 and later worked as an anti-doping figure in professional wrestling .

name: Beef organ / liver diet
summary: Eating beef liver and other organ meats for nutrients; liver is very nutrient-dense but also very high in preformed vitamin A.
lead: Offal, or organ meat, refers to the internal organs of butchered animals such as liver, heart, kidney, tongue and tripe . Attitudes vary: some cultures treat it as taboo and others eat it daily or as a delicacy, and Wikipedia notes that awareness of its nutritional value has grown in places like Ireland, partly through fitness influencers .

name: Deltoid / shoulder implants
summary: Surgical shoulder-contour implants are talked about for width, but no cosmetic studies exist; the research is all joint replacement.
lead: Deltoid or shoulder implants, in the context of looksmaxxing, refers to the idea of surgically placing a solid implant over or within the shoulder region to increase the apparent width or roundness of the shoulders. The deltoid is the muscle that forms the rounded contour of the shoulder and is the prime mover of arm abduction . Broad shoulders are among the proportions discussed in appearance communities as part of a V-shaped upper body.

name: Padded shoulders / structured jackets
summary: Padded shoulders and structured jackets fake shoulder width with tailoring; fashion history backs the look, but no studies test attractiveness effects.
lead: Padded shoulders and structured jackets are a clothing approach used to make the shoulders appear broader and the torso more V-shaped. Fashion shoulder pads are fabric-covered padding sewn inside garments to broaden the look of the shoulders and reduce the appearance of slope . In looksmaxxing communities the practice is discussed as a way to add optical shoulder width without training or surgery.
claims: Shoulder pads add visible width and a more athletic look
Pads can straighten sloping clavicles visually
Padding is a lower-effort substitute that is not worth using if you can build deltoids

name: Horizontal stripes and layering for width
summary: Wearing horizontal stripes and layers to look broader is a styling tactic with no direct studies behind it.
lead: Horizontal stripes and layering are clothing techniques that people in looksmaxxing communities use to make the upper body look broader or bulkier. Layered garments add real volume, and horizontal patterns are said to draw the eye sideways across the chest and shoulders.

name: Gymnastic rings
summary: Suspended rings for bodyweight training; the gymnast physique is the draw, but no studies compare them for looks.
lead: Gymnastic rings are a pair of rings suspended from a frame by straps, used both as an artistic gymnastics apparatus and as a bodyweight training tool. In competition the still rings event is traditionally performed only by male gymnasts because of its demand for upper-body strength . In calisthenics, rings can be used for dips, front and back levers and muscle-ups .

name: Fat Gripz / grip thickeners
summary: Thick rubber grip sleeves sold for forearm work; one acute study exists, none on forearm size.
lead: Fat Gripz are thick rubber sleeves that attach to a barbell, dumbbell or handle to increase its diameter, making it harder to hold. They are used in strength training with the aim of challenging grip and forearm muscles.

name: EMS suit / electrical muscle stimulation
summary: Electrodes that make muscles contract; real in rehab, small trials in fitness, nothing on looks, with rare serious harms reported.
lead: Electrical muscle stimulation (EMS, also called NMES or electromyostimulation) uses electrical impulses delivered through skin electrodes to make muscles contract, and is used in rehabilitation, athletic training and consumer fitness . Whole-body EMS suits apply electrodes across many muscle groups at once and are sold commercially for fitness.

name: Gynecomastia surgery
summary: Surgical removal of excess glandular and fatty chest tissue in men; the established medical route when enlargement persists, with documented complication risks and variable insurance coverage.
lead: Gynecomastia surgery, also called male breast reduction, is a set of operations that remove excess glandular tissue and, often, fat from the male chest. Gynecomastia itself results from an altered balance between estrogen and androgen activity and can arise during puberty, in older age, with certain medications or illnesses, or without an identified cause .

name: Chin tucks
summary: A neck-retraction movement used for posture and deep neck flexor work; most published research concerns swallowing therapy, not jawline appearance.
lead: A chin tuck is a posture or exercise in which the head is retracted backward over the neck so that the chin draws in. In clinical literature the term most often refers to a swallowing maneuver used with people who have dysphagia, and it has been studied with videofluoroscopy and manometry . A resisted version, chin tuck against resistance (CTAR), was proposed as a way to increase activity of the suprahyoid muscles .
claims: Chin tucks improve head posture by stretching the neck.
Prolonged chin-tuck holds can damage the neck.
Sleeping or holding a different head position could improve the jaw.

name: Wall angels
summary: A wall-supported arm-slide drill used for shoulder and upper back mobility and posture; popular in rehab and fitness, with no appearance trials found.
lead: Wall angels, also called wall slides or the V-to-W stretch, are a standing bodyweight exercise in which the arms are slid up and down a wall while the head, upper back, buttocks, elbows and hands stay in contact with it .

name: Thoracic extension over foam roller
summary: A mobility drill that arches the upper back over a foam roller, used to counter rounded posture; no trials of the drill itself were found.
lead: Thoracic extension over a foam roller is a self-mobilization exercise in which the upper back is arched back over a roller. It is used in posture-focused routines for stiffness and a flexed upper back.

name: Hip flexor stretching (couch stretch)
summary: A kneeling quad-and-hip-flexor stretch used to counter anterior pelvic tilt; popular in posture circles, with no trials on that use.
lead: Hip flexor stretching is a flexibility practice aimed at the muscles at the front of the hip, chiefly the iliopsoas and the rectus femoris of the quadriceps. The couch stretch is a popular variation in which the rear knee is placed on the floor with the shin braced up against a couch, wall or bench, so that the hip is held in extension while the front of the thigh is lengthened.

name: Glute bridges / glute activation
summary: A hip-lift exercise used to strengthen the glutes and, in posture circles, to counter anterior pelvic tilt; evidence for that use is absent.
lead: The glute bridge is a floor exercise in which a person lies on their back with knees bent and lifts the hips by contracting the gluteal and hamstring muscles. Related bridge exercises are described by Wikipedia as intended to improve lower back and gluteus strength.  The term glute activation refers to low-load drills such as bridges that are used to switch on the gluteal muscles before heavier training.

name: Anterior pelvic tilt correction
summary: A stretch-and-strengthen routine aimed at tipping the pelvis back to neutral; widely recommended online, thinly referenced and untested for looks.
lead: Anterior pelvic tilt (APT) is described as a posture in which the front of the pelvis drops relative to the back, often accompanied by an exaggerated lower-back arch known as lumbar hyperlordosis.  In looksmaxxing and fitness communities, APT correction refers to a package of stretches and strengthening exercises intended to reduce that tilt, with proponents citing a flatter-looking stomach, better posture and, in some accounts, increased apparent height.

name: Core stability (plank, dead bug)
summary: Plank and dead bug trunk drills pitched for posture and pelvic tilt; broader core-stability research shows modest benefit over general exercise.
lead: Core stability is defined as a person's ability to control the tone, position and movement of the core, meaning the head, neck and torso.  The plank, an isometric hold resembling a push-up position, and the dead bug, a lying limb-movement drill, are common training exercises for it.

name: McGill Big 3
summary: A three-exercise back-sparing core routine tied to biomechanist Stuart McGill; thinly documented here and untested for looks.
lead: The McGill Big 3 is a trio of core exercises, usually described as a modified curl-up, the side bridge and the bird dog, associated with spine biomechanist Stuart McGill. McGill is a Canadian academic and Distinguished Professor Emeritus of Spine Biomechanics at the University of Waterloo, a member of the Order of Canada since 2019 and the author of books including Low Back Disorders and Back Mechanic.

name: Lower trap / serratus work
summary: Exercises for the shoulder-blade muscles used in posture routines; anatomy is well described, appearance benefit untested.
lead: Lower trapezius and serratus anterior work refers to exercises aimed at the muscles that control the shoulder blade (scapula). The lower trapezius pulls the scapula down and helps rotate it upward, while the serratus anterior pulls it forward around the rib cage; together with the upper trapezius they sustain upward rotation for overhead arm movement.

name: Rib flare correction / diaphragm breathing
summary: Breathing and core drills aimed at pulling protruding lower ribs back in; popular in posture circles, with almost no direct trial evidence on appearance.
lead: Rib flare is a descriptive term, used mainly in physical therapy, fitness and posture communities, for lower ribs that protrude outward or forward rather than sitting flush with the abdomen. It is generally described as a postural pattern rather than a disease, although similar-looking rib cage prominence can accompany structural conditions such as scoliosis or pectus excavatum.
claims: Rib flare can be corrected with exercises and breathing retraining
Rib flare comes from weak core and poor breathing mechanics
Exercise can also fix pectus excavatum

name: Jefferson curl
summary: A loaded spinal-flexion mobility exercise popular in strength circles; barely studied, with one small 2026 EMG study to date.
lead: The Jefferson curl is a loaded spinal flexion exercise in which the lifter, standing with a weight, progressively curls the spine forward and down vertebra by vertebra and then reverses the movement. A 2026 paper describes it as having gained popularity in strength and rehabilitation practice but lacking empirical characterisation.
